content:
I noticed that in this job, where only a deep category theory file on galois theory was changed by the new commit, CI failed to get the cache. (Note that CI failed on the prior attempt, but still uploaded a cache for most of Mathlib on my fork, which I was able to fetch and use locally.)

Is this expected for security reasons?

Also tagging @Marcelo Lynch :)
This is the downside of the new scoped-by-SHA behavior of the cache: susbequent commits on the same PR do not share the cache, each push acts as if it were 'the first' and only sees cache from master

Gotcha, as long as it's intentional! :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes: I don't know anything about security but I trust that this is actually a good thing :) (I think actually I knew about this, and then forgot, sorry about that...)
No problem. It's a bad thing for CI perf :-). The point is that this cross-commit sharing would allow a malicious author to poison innocent-looking revisions with earlier-evil-revision-artifacts

@Marcelo Lynch, the new behavior is a major usability regression. Is it possible to mitigate it by allowing the user to mark forks as "trusted"? Eg trusting my own fork would make the new behavior almost indistinguishable from the previous one while providing the same level of security as the new behavior.
@Yaël Dillies You can always use --unsafe to fetch the cache from the latest available commit(s) in your branch history.
We can consider the 'trusted repo' approach as an additional --unsafe option. It's not quite trivial (it needs more metadata in the cache / requests / roundtrips) but it's not terrible either.
I didn't know/overlooked the --unsafe flag, this will do for now thanks!
I'll probably open a PR for the other feature after #41707 is merged
